{'translation': 'Last Friday (the 21st), after the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, during the early morning hours, police escorted a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing onto a police vehicle and took her away. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."'}

{'translation': 'At around 5 a.m. last Friday, over 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates\' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer claimed that a woman in the queue "had what appeared to be a slightly seditious design on her clothing," and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were removing the woman, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying they would "take them to the press area," and extended an orange cordon line towards Ying Wa Street. After the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they packed up the cordon line. A "court-watcher" who was queuing near the woman that day said that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.'}

{'translation': 'When "集誌社" (The Collective) enquired with the police about the reason for the woman being taken away and whether an arrest had been made, the police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was being detained for investigation.'}
